steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for a computer vision paper presenting SecondPose, our method for category-level object pose estimation that fuses DINOv2 semantic features with SE(3)-invariant geometric features. Explain the task, contrast mean-shape priors with semantic priors, describe the method and why our fusion beats direct fusion, and list the contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Category-level pose estimation: task, applications, intra-class shape variation
- Mean shape priors and their failure
- Semantic priors from DINOv2 and how they are used so far
- SecondPose: method overview
- SE(3)-consistent fusion vs direct fusion
- Contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Task
  - full 9 DoF pose: 3D rotation, 3D translation, 3D metric size; arbitrary objects in known categories
  - applications: AR/VR industry (cite), robotics (cite), scene understanding (cite)
  - vs instance-level methods (cite) needing a 3D CAD model per object -> must adapt to shape diversity in a category
  - intra-class shape variation = central focus; real-world objects differ in shape but share a label
- Mean shape vs semantic priors
  - explicit mean shapes as prior (cite)
  - two modules: reconstruct target by slightly deforming mean shape; regress 9D pose from reconstruction (cite) or enhanced intermediate features (cite)
  - assumption: mean shape captures category structure, small deformation enough; false in reality, e.g. chairs with fundamental structural differences
- DINOv2
  - self-supervised large vision models leap; DINOv2 (cite): semantically consistent patch-wise features
  - various methods (cite) use DINOv2 semantics as priors
  - better generalization than category mean shapes: large-scale data, advanced training strategy
  - ZSP (cite): zero-shot semantic correspondences across viewpoints, pose via RANSAC
  - POPE (cite), CNOS (cite): refine detection, implicitly better pose
  - gap: no method fuses DINOv2 with object-specific features for category-level pose directly
- SecondPose
  - SE(3)-Consistent Dual-stream features for Pose estimation
  - DINOv2 patch-wise SE(3)-consistent semantics + two SE(3)-invariant geometric features: pair-wise distance, pair-wise angles
  - hierarchical aggregation in support regions of increasing radius -> local-to-global structure
  - point-aligned with DINOv2 features -> unified representation consistent under SE(3)
  - pipeline: RGB-D -> back-project depth to point cloud -> Geometric and Semantic Streams (Fig. 2.A-B) -> dual-stream fusion (Fig. 2.C) -> SECOND features -> off-the-shelf pose estimator (cite) (Fig. 2.D) -> 9D pose
- SE(3)-consistent vs direct fusion
  - alternative: concatenate DINOv2 features with back-projected points point-wise, no geometric features
  - advantage 1: DINOv2 trained only on RGB; geometric features add local-to-global 3D structure; helps diverse shapes
  - advantage 2: pipeline { point cloud \longrightarrow canonical space } becomes { point cloud \longrightarrow SE(3)-consistent representation \longrightarrow canonical space }; second stage consistent under SE(3) (approximately invariant, see Fig. 4); estimator only works in second stage; more accurate and more efficient
- Contributions (threefold)
  - first method fusing object-specific hierarchical geometric features with semantic DINOv2 features for category-level pose
  - SE(3)-consistent fusion -> unified representation robust under SE(3), suited to downstream pose estimation
  - evaluation: big gains even under severe occlusion and clutter; real-world applications

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Category-level pose estimation means estimating the full 9 degrees-of-freedom (DoF) pose of an object, which includes 3D rotation, 3D translation and 3D metric size, for arbitrary objects that belong to a known set of categories. The task has attracted a lot of research interest because it plays an essential role in many applications, such as the AR/VR industry, robotics and scene understanding. Traditional instance-level pose estimation methods rely on a specific 3D CAD model for each target object, but the category-level approach has to be more adaptable so that it can deal with the shape diversity inside each category. So handling intra-class shape variations has become a central focus. This is crucial for real-world applications, where objects in a category can have very different shapes but still share the same general category label.

Mean Shape vs. Semantic Priors. A common way to handle intra-class shape variation is to use explicit mean shapes as prior knowledge. These methods usually have two functional modules. One reconstructs the target object by slightly deforming the mean shape, and the other regresses the 9D pose from the reconstructed object or from enhanced intermediate features. These methods assume that the mean shape can perfectly capture the structural information of the objects in each category, so that the target object can be reconstructed with minimal deformation. But in reality this assumption does not hold. Objects in the same category, chairs for example, can have fundamental structural differences, and then these methods fail.

Recently self-supervised learning with large vision models has made a big leap forward. Among these, DINOv2 has gotten a lot of attention because it is exceptionally good at providing semantically consistent patch-wise features. Various methods use semantic features from DINOv2 as essential priors for understanding the object. For pose estimation, DINOv2 generalizes better in object representation across each category than category-specific mean shapes do, because of its large-scale training data and advanced training strategy. ZSP uses DINOv2 features directly to build zero-shot semantic correspondences between objects seen from different camera viewpoints, and then it estimates the pose with RANSAC. POPE and CNOS use DINOv2 to refine object detection, which implicitly makes pose estimation more accurate. But as far as we know there is currently no method that looks at how to fuse DINOv2 features with object-specific features to directly improve category-level pose estimation.

- SecondPose
  - DINOv2 SE(3)-consistent semantics + SE(3)-invariant geometric features (pair-wise distance, pair-wise angles)
  - hierarchical aggregation, increasing radius; point-aligned -> unified representation
  - RGB-D -> point cloud -> Geometric and Semantic Streams (Fig. 2.A-B) -> fusion (Fig. 2.C) -> SECOND -> off-the-shelf estimator (Fig. 2.D)
- SE(3)-consistent vs direct fusion
  - direct: concatenate DINOv2 features with back-projected points
  - adv 1: DINOv2 RGB only; add 3D structure
  - adv 2: { point cloud \longrightarrow SE(3)-consistent representation \longrightarrow canonical space }; second stage consistent (Fig. 4); more accurate, more efficient
- Contributions: first fusion method; robust unified representation; gains under occlusion and clutter

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Category-level pose estimation means estimating the full 9 degrees-of-freedom (DoF) pose of an object, which includes 3D rotation, 3D translation and 3D metric size, for arbitrary objects that belong to a known set of categories. The task has attracted a lot of research interest because it plays an essential role in many applications, such as the AR/VR industry, robotics and scene understanding. Traditional instance-level pose estimation methods rely on a specific 3D CAD model for each target object, but the category-level approach has to be more adaptable so that it can deal with the shape diversity inside each category. So handling intra-class shape variations has become a central focus. This is crucial for real-world applications, where objects in a category can have very different shapes but still share the same general category label.

Mean Shape vs. Semantic Priors. A common way to handle intra-class shape variation is to use explicit mean shapes as prior knowledge. These methods usually have two functional modules. One reconstructs the target object by slightly deforming the mean shape, and the other regresses the 9D pose from the reconstructed object or from enhanced intermediate features. These methods assume that the mean shape can perfectly capture the structural information of the objects in each category, so that the target object can be reconstructed with minimal deformation. But in reality this assumption does not hold. Objects in the same category, chairs for example, can have fundamental structural differences, and then these methods fail.

Recently self-supervised learning with large vision models has made a big leap forward. Among these, DINOv2 has gotten a lot of attention because it is exceptionally good at providing semantically consistent patch-wise features. Various methods use semantic features from DINOv2 as essential priors for understanding the object. For pose estimation, DINOv2 generalizes better in object representation across each category than category-specific mean shapes do, because of its large-scale training data and advanced training strategy. ZSP uses DINOv2 features directly to build zero-shot semantic correspondences between objects seen from different camera viewpoints, and then it estimates the pose with RANSAC. POPE and CNOS use DINOv2 to refine object detection, which implicitly makes pose estimation more accurate. But as far as we know there is currently no method that looks at how to fuse DINOv2 features with object-specific features to directly improve category-level pose estimation.

In this paper we present SecondPose, a new method that fuses SE(3)-Consistent Dual-stream features to improve category-level Pose estimation. We use DINOv2's patch-wise SE(3)-consistent semantic features, and we extract two types of SE(3)-invariant geometric features, pair-wise distance and pair-wise angles, to capture object-specific cues. The geometric features are aggregated hierarchically within support regions of increasing radius, which encodes local-to-global information about the object structure. Then these features are point-aligned with the DINOv2 features, giving a unified object representation that is consistent under SE(3) transformations. More concretely, given an RGB-D image of the target object, we first back-project the depth map to get the point cloud. This is fed into our Geometric and Semantic Streams (Fig. 2.A-B), which extract the features for our dual-stream fusion (Fig. 2.C). The fused features, called SECOND, are then fed into an off-the-shelf pose estimator (Fig. 2.D) to regress the 9D pose.

SE(3)-Consistent Fusion vs. Direct Fusion. Another option would be to directly concatenate DINOv2 features with the back-projected points point by point, without extracting SE(3)-invariant geometric features. But the SE(3)-consistent fusion that we propose has two important advantages over this simple approach. First, DINOv2 is only trained with RGB images, so adding geometric features from the point cloud gives it useful local-to-global 3D structural information. This is especially helpful for handling the diverse object shapes within a category. Second, our SE(3)-consistent object representation changes the pose estimation process from { point cloud \longrightarrow canonical space } to { point cloud \longrightarrow SE(3)-consistent representation \longrightarrow canonical space }. In this pipeline the second stage, which goes from our object representation to the human-defined canonical space, is consistent under SE(3) transformations (approximately invariant, see Fig. 4). This makes the pose estimation process much simpler, since the pose estimator only has to work in the second stage. This approach also makes pose estimation more accurate and makes the whole method more efficient.

Our main contributions are threefold:

1. We present SecondPose, the first method that directly fuses object-specific hierarchical geometric features with semantic DINOv2 features for category-level pose estimation.

2. Our SE(3)-consistent dual-stream feature fusion strategy gives a unified object representation that is robust under SE(3) transformations and better suited to downstream pose estimation.

3. Extensive evaluation shows that our SE(3)-consistent fusion strategy improves pose estimation performance a lot, even under severe occlusion and clutter, which makes real-world applications possible.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Category-level pose estimation involves estimating the complete 9 degrees-of-freedom (DoF) object pose, comprising 3D rotation, 3D translation, and 3D metric size, for arbitrary objects within a known set of categories. This task has attracted significant research interest due to its essential role in various applications, including the AR/VR industry [1,2,3,4], robotics [5,6,7], and scene understanding [8,9,10]. Unlike traditional instance-level pose estimation methods [11,12], which rely on specific 3D CAD models for each target object, the category-level approach requires greater adaptability to the inherent shape diversity within each category. Effectively addressing intra-class shape variations has thus become a central focus, which is crucial for real-world applications where objects within a category may differ significantly in shape while sharing the same general category label.

Mean Shape vs. Semantic Priors. One common approach to handling intra-class shape variation is to use explicit mean shapes as prior knowledge [13,14,15]. These methods typically consist of two functional modules: one reconstructs the target object by slightly deforming the mean shape, and the other regresses the 9D pose based on the reconstructed object [14,13] or enhanced intermediate features [15]. They assume that the mean shape can perfectly encapsulate the structural information of objects within each category, so that the target object can be reconstructed with minimal deformation. However, this assumption does not hold in reality. Objects within the same category, such as chairs, may have fundamental structural differences, which causes such methods to fail.

Recently, self-supervised learning with large vision models has made a significant leap forward. Among these models, DINOv2 [16] has gained great attention for its exceptional performance in providing semantically consistent patch-wise features. In particular, various methods [17] use semantic features from DINOv2 as essential priors for understanding the object. In pose estimation, DINOv2 shows superior generalization in object representation across each category compared to category-specific mean shapes, thanks to its large-scale training data and advanced training strategy. ZSP [18] directly leverages DINOv2 features for zero-shot construction of semantic correspondences between objects under different camera viewpoints, and then estimates the pose with RANSAC. POPE [19] and CNOS [20] use DINOv2 to refine object detection, implicitly boosting the accuracy of pose estimation. However, to our knowledge, no existing method explores how to fuse DINOv2 features with object-specific features to directly enhance category-level pose estimation.

In this paper, we present SecondPose, a novel method that fuses SE(3)-Consistent Dual-stream features to enhance category-level Pose estimation. Leveraging DINOv2's patch-wise SE(3)-consistent semantic features, we extract two types of SE(3)-invariant geometric features, pair-wise distance and pair-wise angles, to encapsulate object-specific cues. We hierarchically aggregate geometric features within support regions of increasing radius to encode local-to-global object structure information. These features are then point-aligned with DINOv2 features to form a unified object representation that is consistent under SE(3) transformations. Specifically, given an RGB-D image of the target object, we first back-project the depth map to generate the point cloud, which is then fed into our Geometric and Semantic Streams (Fig. 2.A-B) to extract the features for our dual-stream fusion (Fig. 2.C). The fused features, denoted SECOND, are finally fed into an off-the-shelf pose estimator [21] (Fig. 2.D) to regress the 9D pose.

SE(3)-Consistent Fusion vs. Direct Fusion. Alternatively, one could directly concatenate DINOv2 features with the back-projected points in a point-wise manner, without extracting SE(3)-invariant geometric features. Our proposed SE(3)-consistent fusion, however, holds two important advantages over such a straightforward approach. First, while DINOv2 is trained solely with RGB images, incorporating geometric features from the point cloud enriches it with valuable local-to-global 3D structural information, which is particularly advantageous for handling diverse object shapes within a category. Second, our SE(3)-consistent object representation changes the underlying pose estimation process from { point cloud \longrightarrow canonical space } to { point cloud \longrightarrow SE(3)-consistent representation \longrightarrow canonical space }. In this pipeline, the second stage, from our object representation to the human-defined canonical space, is consistent under SE(3) transformations (approximately invariant, see Fig. 4). This consistency significantly simplifies pose estimation, as the pose estimator only needs to operate within the second stage. This streamlined approach not only improves the accuracy of pose estimation but also contributes to the efficiency of the overall method.

To summarize, our main contributions are threefold:

1. We present SecondPose, the first method to directly fuse object-specific hierarchical geometric features with semantic DINOv2 features for category-level pose estimation.

2. Our SE(3)-consistent dual-stream feature fusion strategy yields a unified object representation that is robust under SE(3) transformations and better suited for downstream pose estimation.

3. Extensive evaluation shows that our SE(3)-consistent fusion strategy significantly boosts pose estimation performance even under severe occlusion and clutter, enabling real-world applications.
